multiplechoiceresponse.p: You want to show how a metric changed month by month for two years. The right chart is:

choice.div: A line chart with time on the horizontal axis.
A pie chart of the twelve months.

div.p: Change over time reads as a line. A pie of months has no order and no trend, and 3-D distorts every comparison.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A bar chart comparing categories should normally:

choice.div: Start the value axis at zero.
Start the axis just below the smallest value, to show the differences.
Use colour as the only way to tell the bars apart.

div.p: Truncating the axis exaggerates differences in a bar chart, because the reader judges bars by length. Colour used alone also excludes colour-blind readers.

choice.div: "12 failures" is meaningless without knowing out of how many.
Percentages are always better than counts.
It makes the chart look fuller.

div.p: A rate needs a base. Report counts and the total together, and give both on the same chart when the base changes.
